title: India Names 26-Member Squad for Historic Friendlies Against Brazil, Uruguay, and Panama
excerpt: Head coach Khalid Jamil picks a blend of experience and emerging talent for three international friendlies against World Cup opposition in September and October.
body:
• Coach Khalid Jamil has named a 26-player squad featuring veterans Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, Anirudh Thapa, and Manvir Singh for three FIFA international friendlies.
  • India will face Panama on September 26 in Bengaluru, followed by five-time world champions Brazil on October 3 and two-time world champions Uruguay on October 6, both in Kolkata.
  • All three opponents competed at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, giving India a rare chance to test against top-tier opposition.
  • Four standby players — including goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwari and midfielder Suresh Singh Wangjam — have been placed on reserve.

The Squad

Indian men's national football team head coach Khalid Jamil announced a 26-player squad on Monday for the September-October FIFA International Match Window, according to the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

The squad includes four goalkeepers, eight defenders, eight midfielders, and six forwards. Veteran goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu leads the keepers alongside Albino Gomes, Prabhsukhan Singh Gill, and Som Kumar. The midfield features captain Anirudh Thapa and the versatile Sahal Abdul Samad, while the forward line is anchored by Manvir Singh, Rahim Ali, and the exciting Vikram Partap Singh.

Notably, Ryan Williams — the Australian-born forward who declared for India — retains his place in the squad after making his debut earlier this year.

"The three matches will provide India with valuable opportunities to test themselves against World Cup opposition, with all three nations having featured at the FIFA World Cup held earlier this year."

— All India Football Federation press release

Three World Cup Opponents Await

The Blue Tigers will open the window against Panama on September 26 at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru. The team then travels to Kolkata for the marquee fixtures — five-time world champions Brazil on October 3 and two-time world champions Uruguay on October 6, both at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan.

All three opponents featured at the 2026 FIFA World Cup held earlier this year, making this window arguably the most ambitious set of friendlies India has ever undertaken. Facing three teams ranked significantly higher offers Jamil's side a chance to benchmark their progress against genuine international quality.

Preparation and Camp Details

Jamil's squad will assemble in Bengaluru on September 14 for a two-week preparatory camp ahead of the Panama fixture. After the opening match, the team will depart for Kolkata on September 28 to prepare for the remaining two encounters.

Four players have been placed on standby and may be drafted into the squad if required: goalkeeper Hrithik Tiwari, defenders Chinglensana Singh Konsham and Roshan Singh Naorem, and midfielder Suresh Singh Wangjam.

Significance for Indian Football

India has historically had limited exposure to elite South American football nations. A match against Brazil, even as a friendly, carries enormous prestige and could attract capacity crowds at the 85,000-seat Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.

For the Indian diaspora, particularly the large communities in the United States, Canada, and the UK, these fixtures represent a moment of pride. The matches are expected to draw significant broadcast attention in diaspora markets.

Full Squad

Goalkeepers: Albino Gomes, Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, Prabhsukhan Singh Gill, Som Kumar

Defenders: Abhishek Singh Tekcham, Akash Mishra, Anwar Ali, Bijoy Varghese, Hmingthanmawia Ralte, Jay Gupta, Pramveer, Ricky Meetei Haobam

Midfielders: Anirudh Thapa, Ashique Kuruniyan, Farukh Choudhary, Lalengmawia Ralte, Macarton Nickson, Mohammed Sanan, Ricky Shabong, Sahal Abdul Samad

Forwards: Edmund Lalrindika, Irfan Yadwad, Manvir Singh, Rahim Ali, Ryan Williams, Vikram Partap Singh

Reserves: Hrithik Tiwari, Chinglensana Singh Konsham, Roshan Singh Naorem, Suresh Singh Wangjam

What to Watch

The September-October window is a critical checkpoint for Jamil, who took charge as head coach after the departure of Igor Stimac. How India competes against three World Cup participants will shape the narrative around the program heading into the 2027 AFC Asian Cup qualifiers. The choice of Bengaluru and Kolkata — two cities with passionate football cultures — signals the AIFF's intent to maximize both atmosphere and commercial impact.
